status.label: Confirm the original text mappings on current stable
status.detail: The original reporter's Alt+1/Alt+2 text mappings failed with Grab and Move enabled; a separate Win+Q report overlaps with open #47585, but the original failure is not established as a duplicate.

judgment.rationale: The original reporter says Alt+1 and Alt+2 text mappings intermittently fail on 0.99.1 while Grab and Move is enabled. They later confirmed persistence when asked about 0.100.2 and found that disabling/re-enabling Grab and Move temporarily restores the mappings. A separate commenter supplied a reproducible Win+Q-to-Alt+F4 failure caused by enabling Keyboard Manager after Grab and Move; that Win-modified hotkey symptom matches open #47585, but it does not cover the original Alt+1/Alt+2 text mappings. Ask the original reporter whether those mappings still fail on v0.102.3001 and whether the Grab and Move toggle remains a workaround; do not mark the entire issue duplicate.
evidence: The original report lists PowerToys 0.99.1 and Alt+1/Alt+2 text mappings that intermittently produce nothing.
The reporter said the failure persisted when asked about 0.100.2 or above, and reported that toggling Grab and Move temporarily restored the mappings.
A separate commenter gave steps for Win+Q-to-Alt+F4 failing when Keyboard Manager is enabled after Grab and Move; enabling Keyboard Manager first works until PowerToys restarts.

Open #47585 tracks Win-modified hotkeys losing effect with Grab and Move configured to Win, and a maintainer reproduced it on 0.100.2; its recorded repro is narrower than the original text mappings here.
The issue has 15 comments, no assignees, and remains open.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether the original Alt+1/Alt+2 text mapping failure still occurs on v0.102.3001 and whether toggling Grab and Move still restores it.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reported text-mapping failure has not been rechecked on current stable, and the related #47585 covers the separate Win-modified hotkey case rather than establishing a covering fix for the original report.

issue_context.summary: The original report's Alt+1/Alt+2 text mappings fail intermittently with Grab and Move enabled; a separate Win-hotkey report is covered by #47585.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.99.1 and says Alt+1/Alt+2 text mappings intermittently enter nothing.
The original reporter confirmed the failure persisted when asked about 0.100.2 or above and found that toggling Grab and Move temporarily restored the mappings.
A separate commenter reports Win+Q-to-Alt+F4 failure when Keyboard Manager is enabled after Grab and Move; restarting PowerToys also reintroduces that failure.
Open #47585 tracks loss of Win-modified hotkeys with Grab and Move using Win; it does not establish a duplicate for the original Alt+1/Alt+2 text-mapping report.
inferences: The original text-mapping failure may involve how Keyboard Manager and Grab and Move initialize or recover, but the reports do not establish whether the same hook-order defect explains both the text and Win-hotkey cases.
issue_context.analysis: Keep the original reporter's Alt+1/Alt+2 failure distinct from the separate Win+Q report already tracked in #47585. The former has a useful workaround and an older-version confirmation, but needs a current-build retest before deeper investigation.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and all 15 comments, including the original reporter's 0.100.2 follow-up and the later Win+Q reproduction.
Compared the separate Win-modified hotkey reproduction with open #47585; that narrower case is covered, while the original text mappings remain distinct.

comment.body: Thanks for confirming that your Alt+1/Alt+2 text mappings persisted as a problem on 0.100.2 and that toggling Grab and Move temporarily restored them. Could you retest those original text mappings on v0.102.3001 with Grab and Move enabled, and say whether toggling Grab and Move still restores them and whether a PowerToys restart brings the failure back? The later Win+Q report is tracked separately in #47585, so this retest is specifically about your text mappings.
